subject: General Science
title: Linear Motion

outcomes.text: explain terms used in linear motion,
calculate variables of motion using equations of linear motion with constant acceleration,
investigate the effect of gravity on bodies under free fall,
appreciate the significance of linear motion and free fall in real life.

content: Equations of linear motion (no derivations needed),
Examples of linear motion with constant acceleration
inquiry_questions: How is free fall motion important in real life?
How can the dangers of free fall in our day to day life be mitigated?
suggested_learning_experiences: Discuss with peers the meaning and differences between the terms used in linear motion (distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration).
Use digital devices/print media to research on the equations of linear motion.
Solve numerical problems in linear motion with constant acceleration using equations of linear motion.
Discuss with peers the applications of linear motion in real life and present in plenary.
Drop objects from a certain height to observe the increase in speed of the objects and infer the effect of gravity on objects.
Observe safety measures when dropping objects to investigate the effect of gravity on objects.
Discuss the dangers of accelerating on sloping surfaces such as steeply sloping roads.
Discuss with peers the safety measures put in real-life situations to minimise fatal injuries resulting from free fall.
Carry out assignments on examples of bodies under free-fall motion.
coreCompetencies:
Communication and collaboration: as the learner works with peers to discuss and present in plenary the application of linear motion in real life.
Learning to learn: as the learner carries out assignments on examples of bodies under free-fall motion and presents the findings in a group discussion.
values:
Peace: the learner displays tolerance and calmness when discussing the application of linear motion in real life.
Unity: the learner displays cooperation and collaboration with others while investigating the effect of gravity on objects.
pcis:
Road safety: increased awareness on how to minimise fatal injuries resulting from road crashes on sloping roads using the concept of free fall of objects.
Life Skills Education (self-awareness): the learner observes safety measures when dropping objects to investigate the effect of gravity on objects.
transcription_policy: Source wording retained;line breaks/bullets normalised;pixels authority.
notes: No lesson allocation is stated in this table; do not use the inventory baseline count as an official allocation.
Any falling-object investigation must use a low, controlled drop area and teacher-approved light objects, with exclusion zones; never drop objects from buildings, onto roads, people or vehicles.

Ideal free-fall equations assume negligible air resistance; real observations with ordinary objects can differ, which should be stated rather than presented as a direct measurement of ideal free fall.
